items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...we talked about Uncle Tommy and Dizzy has something from his autobiography... Do you agree with what he said? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. I have to agree.

ctx.x: You know, that's a hell of a come up when you think about black men and women spending their money on Canal Street in the 40s and 50s and they didn't have bathroom facilities. You had to find your service station someplace, I hate to say a back alley, because a lot of black people were cultured and they wouldn't do that. They would probably go to the bathroom before coming home. You know.

This is the thing from, this is from Dizzy Gillespie's, we talked about Uncle Tommy and Dizzy has something from his autobiography to be or not to Bob and Dizzy's your age, so him making this, he says, he says, I had my own way of Tommy. Every generation of blacks in slavery has had to develop its own way of Tommy, of accommodating itself to a basically unjust situation. Do you agree with what he said?
